english.title: Cause another person to deposit or incinerate at sea without licence
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) caused **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to do something for which a licence was needed under Part II of the Food and Environment Protection Act 1985, namely **(..SPECIFY ACTION FOR WHICH LICENCE NEEDED..) other than in pursuance of such a licence and in accordance with its provisions in that **(..SPECIFY NATURE OF NON-COMPLIANCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 9(1)(b) and 21(2A) of the Food and Environment Protection Act 1985.

english.notes:
It shall be a defence for a person charged with an offence in relation to any operation to prove -
(a) that the operation was carried out for the purpose of securing the safety of a vessel, aircraft, hovercraft or marine structure or of saving life; and (b) that he took steps within a reasonable time to inform one or other of the Ministers -

(i) of the operation;
(ii) of the locality and the circumstances in which it took place; and (iii) of any substances or articles concernedA person does not have the defence provided above if the court is satisfied -
(a) that the operation -(i) was not necessary for any purpose mentioned in paragraph (a) of that subsection; and (ii) was not a reasonable step to take in the circumstances; or(b) that it was necessary for one of those purposes but the necessity was due to the fault of the defendantIt shall be a defence for a person charged with an offence under section 9(1) in relation to an operation to prove that -(a) for the purposes of paragraph 23 of the electronic communications code (undertaker's works), the person is the operator or a relevant undertaker and,
(b) the activity was carried out for the purpose of executing emergency works, within the meaning of that code.In this subsection 'the electronic communications code' means the code set out in Schedule 2 to the Telecommunications Act 1984.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding fifty thousand pounds
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
